note: The walker's figure (doc 23, W5; approved October 21, 2026): Matt's Meshy model, split into a body and two arms in nTop and coloured per vertex by tools/figure-prep/prep.py (assets/figures/walker.glb). The rest pose is the A-pose: the arms hang down by the rig. Metres, y up, body +z forward, feet on y = 0. bones: name, parent, pivot (the arms' pivots come from the model's extras, so a new prep moves them). skin: where each part blends between bones, as anchors along a height (y) or along the arm (t, m out from the shoulder). hang: the arms' resting direction. gait: per pace, step length, foot lift, arm swing, lean and the rise and fall of the hips; wade blends in by the water's depth. springs: the hat tip, coat skirt and pack follow a beat late (stiffness per second squared, damping 0..1 of critical). eyes: the two ovals the shader draws on the head (rest pose), their colour, a faint glow after dark (cd per m2), blinks and expressions. poses: sit, kneel, feed, the arrivals, and the keeper's camp acts (crawl, drink, pitch, lay, strike, crawlIn, climbOut; see actsNote). All motion is drawing only: it reads the walker and never changes it.

body.note: What the creature pass reads: the soft contact shadow (scaleReal sizes it, times displayScale), displayScale: the figure is drawn this much of the model (October 21, 2026: 0.737, so you stand 1.4 m tall, not 1.9 m, and creatures read larger beside you; the eyes, contact shadow and all the motion (gait, poses, ground under the feet) follow it, src/world/figure/motion.js works in body meters), the cloth's sheen (none) and the eye bones for a wet glint (none: the eyes are drawn).

gait.note: Paces by speed in body meters a second (the walker's speed divided by body.displayScale, so a smaller figure takes a longer pace for its size and quicker steps); stepM, liftM and the rest are body meters too. The figure blends between them by the speed it is given. stance: share of a stride a foot is down (each pace may set its own; under a half both feet leave the ground between steps). The stroll (1.5 m/s, about 2.0 body m/s) keeps the 1.5 pace; above it the walk turns into a jog (2.9) and a run (3.7, the hurry speed of 2.7 m/s): a longer stride, a flight phase, more forward lean, a bent-elbow arm pump, and bobM below 0, so the hips are lowest over the planted foot and highest in flight, which bounces the hat tip and the pack (Phase 1 fix F11). tipDeg and carryDeg: how far the body tips forward setting off and carries on forward stopping, at that pace (see lean); wade blends toward its own.

arms.note: The walking arm swing's shape (the swing itself is each pace's armDeg). elbowForward: radians of extra elbow bend per radian of forward swing; elbowBack: how much the elbow straightens on the back swing, the same way; across: how far a forward swing comes in across the body, per radian of swing.

springs.note: The parts that follow a beat late. hatTip.accelGain: how far the tip tips back as you speed up (and forward as you stop). skirt.strideSway: how far the coat skirt swings to the side of the forward knee, per meter the knees are apart front to back; skirt.speedFlare: how far it flares back per body meter a second. pack.tiltGain: radians the pack tips per meter it lags the body's rise and fall; pack.rock: share of the hips' twist the pack rocks with.

lean.note: Leaning into starts and stops (walker gestures, part 1; October 24, 2026; src/world/figure/lean.js): the standing lean (the pace's, or a little at rest) follows a soft spring, with extra pulls. Speeding up pulls it toward the pace's tipDeg (full at accelRef, body m/s2; the walker eases up at 2.5 m/s2, about 3.4 body m/s2); slowing down pulls it toward carryDeg (full at brakeRef), the body carrying on as the feet brake. stiffness per second squared; damping (share of critical) while moving, settleDamping once stopped, so the walking lean easing off as you stop swings back just past upright once and settles. The pace is read at the speed you were going, falling off over cruiseFallS.

look.note: Where the walker looks (walker gestures, part 2; October 24, 2026; src/world/figure/look.js). The head turns up to maxYawDeg and tips up or down up to maxPitchDeg in all (a posture's and an act's tip included); toward a thing it tips pitchShare of the way, up to targetPitchDeg, so the face stays in view and the eyes look the rest; the chest takes chestShare of a turn and what is past the head's limit, up to chestMaxDeg. Both ease on springs (headStiffness, chestStiffness per second squared, never faster than degPerS) and turn walkingLess less while walking. What it looks at, first wins by weight over (1 + distance times distFalloff): kinds.focus, the thing you clicked or are about to use (held focusS); kinds.arrival, a creature that just arrived (worth a look for arrivalS); the fire, a creature close by, a find. Each only within its maxM and within frontDeg of straight ahead (never behind you). A choice holds at least holdS and gives way only to one switchRatio better; a passing interest is looked at for its dwellS, then left be for againS. sameM: how far a thing may move and still be the same thing. liftM: how far over the ground it is looked at. eyes: the drawn eyes lead the head (it starts headDelayS after them), shifting up to shiftM (m across the face, x and y) by how far the head and chest still are from the thing (full at fullDeg), on a quick spring.

footprints.note: Prints (W6): each step that lands on sand, or on bare earth and mud, leaves a soft print the shape of the boot's sole, darkening the ground by darkness; it fades over fadeH game hours, and is gone once the tide covers it. Not on grass or rock (minWeight: how much of the ground must be sand or soil), not under water deeper than dryM. Never saved: the island forgets you between visits. soleM is in world meters, set for the 1.4 m figure (0.737 of the model). max: how many at once (the oldest go first).

grass.note: Grass underfoot (W6): blades lean away from the walker and press a little flatter: under the body within bodyM (sitM when sitting), and where each of the last steps landed within footM, springing back over springS seconds. World meters, set for the 1.4 m figure (0.737 of the model).

kneel.note: One knee down, worked out from the leg's lengths (motion.js): the left knee rests kneeM above the ground, kneeBackM behind the hip and kneeOutM out from it; the hips come pelvisZ forward over it (the weight forward) and sit as low as the thigh allows; the shin lies back to the tucked toes, the ankle toeM up. front: the right foot planted [x, z]. maxDropM: how far an act may sink the hips while kneeling. leanDeg, headDeg: the back and head lean toward the work.

poses.actsNote: The keeper's camp acts (docs/future/13-keepers-camp.md 2.3; October 22, 2026), played by walk.act(name) and src/world/figure/acts.js. posture: the walker's posture while it plays (for presence and the view); after: its posture once done. keys: at t seconds in, kneel and crawl (0..1, how far into each posture), lean and head (extra degrees forward and down; negative leans back or looks up), drop (the hips lower, body m), arms (0..1, how much the hands follow l and r) and l, r (where the left and right hand reach, body m: x left, y over the ground under you, z ahead). A key changes only what it names; the rest carries on from the key before, easing between. The last key's t is the act's length, and walk:act-done comes then. crawl: the hands-and-knees pose crawlIn ends in, held until climbOut or a walk (hipDeg tips the hips, pelvisZ brings them forward over the knees). ease.actInS: an act blends in from the posture it began in; ease.stepLiftM: a foot that moves far as the posture changes lifts this high on the way, a step and not a slide.

gestures.note: A short gesture for each thing the walker does by hand (walker gestures, part 3; October 24, 2026; src/world/figure/acts.js), played by walk.gesture(name, spot) or by the action itself. The same keys as the camp acts (kneel, lean, head, drop, arms, l, r), plus yaw (the head's extra turn, degrees to the left), but a gesture plays over the walker's posture: its kneel takes the figure down at least that far, it never stops a walk or a tap, and a walk fades it out over ease.gestureFadeS. Given a spot, the walker turns to face it and looks at it first. gather: kneel, reach to the ground, pinch, bring the handful up to the pouch at the hip. setDown: reach back to the pack, bring the pouch round, bend and lower it onto the pile. takeUp: bend, scoop with both hands, lift it over the shoulder into the pack. heapHere: a small bend, the hand opens at your feet. empty: hold the pouch out, tip it, a little shake. lift (a log or stone, L3a): kneel, both hands under the edge, heave it up, hold while it is up (under-log lift.holdS), lower it back. feedFire: kneel, toss a stick in, both hands out to the warmth. netSet: kneel, lay the net forward with both arms; netLift: pull it up hand over hand. rise: getting up from a kneel or a seat, a lean forward and a hand pushing on the knee. stuck: a look left and right (walks: it plays on as you walk off, not faded). sow: planting and placing gifts on foot (D1a): the right hand dips to the hip pouch, then one quick flick forward and up toward the clicked spot, the seed leaving the hand at sowing.json flickS (0.32 s), once a click. make (S1, October 24, 2026): kneeling at the workbench, both hands work at its top (about 0.6 m): a twist with one hand, then the other, pull the binding tight, settle, and up; as long as cook.json makeS.
